title: Equal areas in equal times
lede: A planet circles a star on an ellipse, its position found by solving Kepler's equation. The two shaded wedges are swept in equal amounts of time. The arrow shows its speed.
notice: The planet races past the star and crawls far away. The arrow is longest at the closest point.
Wedge A is short and wide at its tip, wedge B long and thin, yet the two areas printed below match to four decimals.
At eccentricity 0 the orbit is a circle, the speed ratio stays at 1, and both wedges are identical.
hint: Drag to tilt the view. Raise the eccentricity and watch the speed.
